before:
Allotment Society — Draft Minutes, Spring General Meeting

Twenty-eight members attended, with the chair presiding. The accounts were received without question. On the water motion, the vote was nineteen in favour and nine against, and the motion as carried sets the annual water levy at twelve pounds per plot. Two members asked that invoices go out before the end of May, and the treasurer agreed. The hedge contract was renewed with the same firm for one further year. Under any-other-business the chair thanked the outgoing plot warden. These minutes are circulated in draft; corrections of fact should reach the secretary within fourteen days, after which the minutes stand adopted.
after:

before:
Harbour Notes — Weekly Bulletin

Visiting craft continue to arrive ahead of the regatta. Readers have asked what the harbour byelaws currently require of tenders after dark: the byelaw in force requires a white all-round light on any tender under way between sunset and sunrise. The harbourmaster's office confirms no change to that provision is before the council this season. Fuel prices at the pontoon rose by two pence a litre on Monday. The dredger returns to the outer channel next month, and the east pontoon will close for two mornings while anodes are replaced. Contributions for next week's bulletin should reach the office by Thursday noon.
after:
Harbour Notes — Weekly Bulletin

Visiting craft continue to arrive ahead of the regatta. Readers have asked what the harbour byelaws currently require of tenders after dark: the byelaw in force requires a white all-round light on any tender under way at all times when afloat. The harbourmaster's office confirms no change to that provision is before the council this season. Fuel prices at the pontoon rose by two pence a litre on Monday. The dredger returns to the outer channel next month, and the east pontoon will close for two mornings while anodes are replaced. Contributions for next week's bulletin should reach the office by Thursday noon.
variation_site: In the byelaw sentence, the stated period during which the light requirement applies.
author_note: Corrects the bulletin's description of the byelaw in force; no provision changes.

before:

before:
Depot Working Arrangements

These arrangements apply to all crews working out of the north depot. Vehicles are fuelled at the end of each shift, not the start. Defect cards go to the workshop window before the driver leaves the yard. Invoices from subcontractors are submitted within thirty days of the work being done. Visitors wait at the barrier until a crew member walks them in. The kitchen is cleared by whoever used it last. Where these arrangements and a written contract differ, the contract governs. Questions go to the yard supervisor, whose decision stands until the next depot meeting.
after:

before:
Staff Handbook — Leaving Us

This page answers the questions people most often ask when they decide to move on. How much notice do I give? Staff give four weeks' notice in writing to their line manager. Can I take untaken holiday during notice? Usually, by agreement with your manager; otherwise it is paid out. When is my last pay run? The month you leave, on the usual date, with any adjustments the following month. Do I return equipment before the last day? Yes, to the facilities desk, which will sign it back in. The tone of this page is informal, but it is part of your terms and is applied as written.
after:

before:
Workshop Ladder Care

Ladders in the workshop are numbered and live on the south wall rack. Ladders are inspected monthly and the tag on the stile shows the last inspection date. A ladder with a missing or out-of-date tag is taken out of use and laid flat behind the rack until it is inspected. Footwear with worn soles is not used on ladders. The tallest ladder is a two-person carry. Damage found mid-job is reported the same day, and the ladder comes out of use at once, whatever the tag says. This notice is part of the workshop's safe system of work and is enforced as such.

before:
Small Craft Register — Entry 214

Entry 214 records a seven-metre wooden sloop, carvel-built, single mast, lifted each winter. The craft is registered under the name Merle from the date of this entry, all previous entries notwithstanding. The keeper of the register notes the hull survey of last spring remains attached and unamended. Mooring: river frontage, berth eleven. The registered keeper is unchanged. Under the register's rules, the name recorded in the current entry is the craft's name for all purposes of the register; painted names, former names, and names in private use have no standing here.

before:
County Herbarium — Accepted Names List, Entry 88

Entry 88 covers the meadow population first vouchered in 1962, with specimens re-examined twice since. For the purposes of this list, the population is carried under the genus Ranunculus, following the county recorder's adoption of the current national checklist. The vouchers themselves are unchanged, and no character of the plants is re-described in this entry: leaf, flower, and seed notes stand exactly as written on the sheets. Localities and dates are as vouchered. Where field guides and this list differ, recorders submitting to the county database use the name as carried here, so that records made in different decades fall under one heading.

Library Catalogue — Record 4471

Nothing about the volume itself is altered by this record: pagination, binding, and provenance notes stand as previously entered. Readers should note the author's foreword is bound after the index in this copy, an oddity of the rebinding. Loans are reference-only, as for all closed-stack items. before:
Churchyard Survey — Field Notes, Second Visit

The second visit covered the north half, in dry weather with good light. The boundary wall is sound apart from two loose copings by the gate. The large tree at the lychgate is an English oak, measured at three metres' girth at chest height. Seventeen headstones were photographed and their inscriptions logged; three are now illegible beyond the first line. The path edging noted as lifting in the first visit has been re-set. No new subsidence was seen. These notes describe what was found on the day; nothing here directs any work, which is for the council's contractor list in the usual way.

before:
Incident Note — Yard Gate, Tuesday Morning

At about half past eight the inward gate was struck while opening. The vehicle involved was a delivery van, which stopped at once; the driver stayed and gave details. The gate arm is bent but the motor runs, and the gate has been left latched open pending repair. No one was hurt, and no load was carried across the walkway at the time. The camera over the gate was recording and the file has been copied to the incident folder. This note records the morning's events as observed; the repair itself will be raised separately through the maintenance system in the ordinary way.

before:
High Street Walkabout — Notes for the Newsletter

The walkabout took in both sides of the street between the bridge and the clock. The corner unit by the bridge is a pharmacy, open six days, with the awning newly recovered. Mid-terrace, the two vacant units remain vacant, though one has a fitting-out notice in the window. The bakery smell reported by readers comes from the unit behind the arcade, not the arcade itself. Bunting from the spring fair is still up at the clock end and looks tired. These notes describe the street as walked on the day; whether anything should be done about any of it is for the committee's agenda, not this page.
